what: Interesting spots for a live look: fast-moving stars and long-period variables
source: Gaia DR3 (ESA/Gaia/DPAC) via the ESA Gaia archive; positions moved to 2026.0 by proper motion

spots.name: Kapteyn's Star
spots.note: A red dwarf from the Milky Way's halo, crossing the sky at about 8.6 arcseconds a year.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 4810594479418041856 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Groombridge 1830
spots.note: An old halo star with one of the largest proper motions known.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 4034171629042489088 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Lacaille 9352
spots.note: A nearby red dwarf, 10.7 light years away, moving almost 7 arcseconds a year.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 6553614253923452800 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Teegarden's Star
spots.note: A small, faint red dwarf with planets, 12.5 light years away.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 35227046884571776 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Wolf 359
spots.note: One of the Sun's nearest neighbours, a dim red dwarf 7.9 light years away.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 3864972938605115520 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Lalande 21185
spots.note: One of the brightest red dwarfs in the sky, 8.3 light years away.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 762815470562110464 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: 61 Cygni A
spots.note: The first star whose distance was measured (Bessel, 1838).
spots.source: Gaia DR3 1872046609345556480 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Luyten's Star
spots.note: A red dwarf 12 light years away with a planet in its habitable zone.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 3139847906307949696 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Van Maanen's Star
spots.note: The nearest solitary white dwarf, a burnt-out star core.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 2552928187080872832 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Proxima Centauri
spots.note: The nearest star to the Sun, 4.2 light years away.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 5853498713190525696 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Ross 128
spots.note: A quiet red dwarf 11 light years away, with an Earth-sized planet.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 3796072592206250624 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Mira
spots.note: The original long-period variable: it brightens and fades over about 11 months.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 2493390319631956352 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)

spots.name: Chi Cygni
spots.note: A Mira variable with one of the largest brightness swings of any star.
spots.source: Gaia DR3 2034702312280673792 (position and proper motion; position moved to 2026.0)
